title: post-incident-learning-codex-handoff-and-synthesis-2025
author: Maya Rodriguez
body:
Post‑Incident Learning Codex: Handoff, Synthesis, and Customer Briefing Patterns

Summary
This playbook documents a standardized, auditable process for converting operational incidents into durable organizational learning. It covers immediate triage-to-handoff checklists for on‑call rotations, artifact collection and retention, a concise postmortem cadence, and reusable customer communication templates. The goal is faster restoration during incidents, higher quality postmortems, and improved readiness across rotations.

Scope
- Applies to all production incidents impacting Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated services (latency, errors, throughput, availability).
- Not for design discussion artifacts (those belong in product-docs).
- Includes guidance for private deployments when Redwood support is the primary responder.

Goals
- Ensure every incident produces a minimal, searchable artifact set within 24 hours.
- Drive a 25% reduction in repeat incidents for the same root cause class within 6 months.
- Shorten the time to first customer notification to 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2 events.

Ownership & Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, owns timelines and customer comms until handoff.
- Bridge Operator: maintains the incident bridge (Slack channel, Zoom), updates status page and artifacts.
- Postmortem Owner: drafts the postmortem and assigns action items within 72 hours.
- Documentation Steward: ensures runbooks and KB entries are updated postmortem.
- Customer Liaison: handles external customer messages and escalations.

Triggering events (examples)
- SLO breach: 99th percentile latency > 500ms for 5 consecutive minutes for model inference endpoint.
- Error spike: 5x baseline 5xx rate sustained for > 10 minutes.
- Capacity constraint: GPU pool utilization > 90% with queue > 60s for > 5 minutes.
- Data plane failure: inability to reach KV cache across region.

Immediate (first 0–30 minutes) checklist
1. IC acknowledges incident and posts summary to bridge with: Impact, Hypothesis, First actions, Owner list.
2. Bridge Operator opens standard bridge channel: #bridge-incident-YYYYMMDD and pins these artifacts: runbook used, SLO dashboard link, status page draft.
3. Triage responders collect a quick snapshot (commands below) and upload to incident artifacts bucket.
4. Customer Liaison drafts and sends Initial Status (template in Templates section) within 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2.
5. If degradation continues past 30 minutes, IC escalates to senior oncall and notifies SRE lead.

Snapshot commands (run immediately)
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference > /tmp/incident-pods.txt
- kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference --since=10m > /tmp/incident-logs-10m.txt
- curl -s 'https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(request_latency_ms[5m])' > /tmp/latency-metrics.json
- redis-cli -h cache-01.redwood.local INFO > /tmp/redis-info.txt

Handoff checklist (shift or ownership transfers)
- Time of handoff (ISO 8601)
- Summary of what’s known and what’s being worked
- Active mitigations and why they matter
- Remaining risks and what to test next
- Where artifacts are stored (S3 path or Confluence page)
- Postmortem Owner assigned (name + ETA for draft)
- Communication status: customers notified? internal comms sent?

Post‑incident artifact checklist (minimal required set)
- Incident timeline (UTC) with 1‑minute granularity where available
- Bridge chat export (Slack/Zoom transcript)
- Snapshot files (pods, logs, metrics, redis/info) and collector commands used
- Runbooks invoked (link + version)
- SLO dashboards and alert graphs (PNG)
- Final incident commander notes (hypothesis and key decisions)
- Customer messages and support ticket IDs

Artifact naming and storage convention
- S3 path: s3://incidents/YYYY/MM/DD/incident-<short-id>-<service>/
- Files: <timestamp>-<service>-<artifact-type>.log or .png (example: 2025-03-18T15:12Z-inference-pods.txt)
- Confluence: page title: "Incident <short-id> — <service> — Brief"

Postmortem cadence and expectations
- 24 hours: IC publishes incident brief in Confluence with timeline and artifact links.
- 72 hours: Postmortem Owner posts first draft with root cause hypothesis and corrective actions.
- 7 business days: Postmortem final draft complete, actions assigned and scheduled.
- 30 days: Follow-up review to validate fixes and close action items.

Postmortem structure (minimum required sections)
1. Summary (one paragraph)
2. Impact (users, customers, SLOs)
3. Timeline (ordered events, UTC)
4. Root cause analysis (evidence-backed)
5. Corrective actions (owner, ETA, verification steps)
6. Preventative actions (what changed in runbooks/SRE playbooks)
7. Lessons learned and TL;DR for execs

Prioritization rubric for corrective actions
- P0: fixes required to restore SLOs or remove single points of failure (implement within 7 days)
- P1: prevent recurrence for the same customer class (30 days)
- P2: documentation, observation, or low-effort reliability improvements (90 days)

Customer communication templates (copy/paste, replace placeholders)
Initial status (to be sent within 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2):
"We are investigating elevated error rates and increased latency for the inference API in <region>. Impact: some requests may fail or be delayed. Current hypothesis: cache mismatch between autoscaled pools. Next update: <ETA or time>. Incident ID: <incident-id>. Contact: <support-email>"

Ongoing status (every 30–60 minutes until resolved):
"Update: We are currently applying an increase in capacity and validating request queue drain. Impact: ~<percent>% of requests affected. Mitigation steps taken: <list>. Next update: <ETA>. Incident ID: <incident-id>"

Resolved notice (after full verification):
"Resolved: The issue affecting inference latency and errors in <region> has been resolved as of <time> UTC. Root cause: <short cause>. Customer impact: <summary>. Follow-up: A postmortem will be published at <link> within 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, please contact <support-contact>."

On‑call cross‑training and knowledge retention
- Shadowing requirement: every new oncall must complete 3 shadowed incidents and run 2 sandbox drills in the first 60 days.
- Mini‑game days: monthly 90‑minute scenarios run by SRE lead; attendance required for oncall rotation.
- Playbook updates: Documentation Steward to update runbook within 5 business days after postmortem if a procedural change is required.

Game day and training schedule template
- Week 1: Intro & tooling (1h) – dashboard walkthrough, artifact collection commands.
- Week 2: Simulated silent degradation scenario (2h) – focus on detection and customer comms.
- Week 3: Bridge ops and status page drills (1h) – practice templates and automation.
- Week 4: Deep dive retro (1h) – review simulated incident and update runbooks.

Automation & validation hooks
- On bridge creation, a bot auto-generates: incident short-id, S3 artifact path, and drafts initial status with the template.
- Runbook verification job (nightly) executes smoke checks and records pass/fail in the incident artifacts bucket.
- Postmortem checklist automation: a GitHub actions workflow creates issues for each corrective action with labels and due dates.

SLOs and thresholds referenced in this playbook
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inference 99p latency (regional) | 99% <= 300ms | 99p > 500ms for 5m |
| Inference error rate (5xx) | <= 0.5% | 5xx > 1.5% baseline*5 for 10m |
| GPU pool utilization | N/A | util > 90% and queue > 60s for 5m |

*Baseline calculated as 30‑day rolling mean.

Success metrics for the playbook
- Time to initial customer notice: target < 15 minutes (measured across SEV1/SEV2 incidents).
- Postmortem completion rate: 95% of incidents have a draft within 72 hours.
- Action closure rate: 80% of P0/P1 items closed or scheduled within 30 days.

Retention, tagging and searchability
- All incident artifacts must include tags: incident-id, service, region, severity, postmortem-owner.
- Confluence pages must include the label: incident-archive and the S3 path for artifacts.
- Search tip: use the incidents index (Confluence macro) or query the S3 index with the incident-id prefix.

Appendix A — Minimal incident timeline example
- 2025-03-18T15:12Z: Alert fired – inference-99p latency > 500ms.
- 2025-03-18T15:14Z: Bridge opened, initial status published.
- 2025-03-18T15:20Z: Cache cluster restart attempt, partial improvement.
- 2025-03-18T15:48Z: Autoscale policy invoked; queue draining begins.
- 2025-03-18T16:10Z: 99p latency back under threshold; monitoring for regression.

Appendix B — Postmortem quick checklist (one‑page)
- [ ] Publish incident brief (24h)
- [ ] Assign Postmortem Owner (72h)
- [ ] Draft corrective actions with owners and ETAs (72h)
- [ ] Schedule 30‑day follow up to validate fixes
- [ ] Update runbooks and label changes in Confluence
